definitions: To suddenly worsen or become more active after a period of being stable or dormant, especially in reference to a disease, an argument, or a fire.
To erupt or intensify quickly and often unexpectedly.
examples: Her allergies tend to flair up in the spring.
The old injury might flair up if you overexert yourself.
Tensions between the two groups flared up again last night.
The fire flared up when the wind picked up.
